response.passage: Welcome to the City Zoological Park FAQ. Q: Who manages the park? A: Mr. Rajesh Sharma oversees daily operations, while the City Council handles the budget. Q: Why are the nocturnal enclosures kept dark during the day? A: Because the animals are active at night, we dim the lights to mimic their natural habitat. Q: How many species are currently housed here? A: We have 42 distinct species, including the rare Bengal Tiger. Q: Can visitors feed the animals? A: No, feeding is strictly prohibited because improper food causes digestive distress in our residents. Q: When was the park founded? A: The park was established in 1994, following a donation from the Gupta family. Q: Is the park open on public holidays? A: Yes, we remain open every day except for Republic Day, when the staff takes a break. Q: What should I do if I lose my belongings? A: Please report to the main office near the entrance. Q: Are there guided tours available? A: Yes, Mrs. Sunita Rao leads group tours every Saturday morning for students. Q: Why do the lions roar so loudly? A: They roar to mark their territory against other predators in the vicinity.
response.summary: This FAQ provides essential information about the City Zoological Park's management, operations, and visitor rules. It highlights specific policies regarding animal care, park history, and available visitor services.
